# 191 · A cent too much per item, refuted at the route and in the kernel, no inferred mapping absorbing it

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **✗ Violation: counterexample found** | functional | high | refactor, behaviour change not intended | [`Pricing#total`](../../examples/apps/shop/src/main/java/shop/Pricing.java) | [B9: Regression verification](../../lib/README.md) |

> The value-object refactor of 190, with `total` charging one cent more per item. The input mapping `old.cents == new.amount.cents + 1` would make the totals agree, is not vacuous and is even a bijection, and it would hide the regression; the tool never proposes it. The route and the kernel's `total` are both refuted on one cent for one item, each witness replayed on the JVM.

Tags: [payments](../README.md#tag-payments), [spring-boot](../README.md#tag-spring-boot), [off-by-one](../README.md#tag-off-by-one), [joint-run](../README.md#tag-joint-run), [object-inputs](../README.md#tag-object-inputs), [own-checker](../README.md#tag-own-checker)

## The change

`Quote`'s amount, a `long` of cents, becomes a value object, `Money`, so `Quote(long cents, int quantity)` is now `Quote(Money amount, int quantity)`; `Pricing.total` reads `q.amount.cents()` where it read `q.cents`; the pure helper `Pricing.discount` (a tenth off ten items or more) is rewritten as an early return; and the route `POST /quotes` makes the quote with `new Money(cents)`. Nothing is meant to change: not the total, not the event the route sends, not what `Pricing.withQuantity` hands back. In this version `total` also adds a cent to the amount before multiplying: `(q.amount.cents() + 1) * q.quantity`.

**Before** ([`Pricing.java`](../../examples/apps/shop/src/main/java/shop/Pricing.java), line 1):

```java
package shop;

/** The pricing kernel. */
public final class Pricing {
    private Pricing() {}

    /** A tenth off an order of ten items or more. */
    static long discount(long gross, int quantity) {
        return quantity >= 10 ? gross / 10 : 0;
    }

    public static long total(Quote q) {
        long gross = q.cents * q.quantity;
        return gross - discount(gross, q.quantity);
    }
```

**After:**

```java
package shop;

/** The pricing kernel, over money. */
public final class Pricing {
    private Pricing() {}

    /** A tenth off an order of ten items or more, written the other way round: the changed pure helper. */
    static long discount(long gross, int quantity) {
        if (quantity < 10) return 0;
        return gross / 10;
    }

    public static long total(Quote q) {
        long gross = (q.amount.cents() + 1) * q.quantity;
        return gross - discount(gross, q.quantity);
    }
```

## What the verifier found

The two builds disagree on `shop.Pricing#total`. The checker found this input, and the verifier replayed it on the JVM against both builds (an entry point under the same recording stubs, a kernel method with its objects made by their constructors):

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `total(q=new Quote(new Money(0), 1))` | `0` | `1` |

The domain is `q: a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(amount: Money(cents: long), quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts; in the previous version, a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(cents: long, quantity: int), from the new q's amount.cents and quantity as the correspondence's input equations say (old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents, old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity), and satisfying them`.

Every part the run checked, nothing written by hand (the entry points under their observation specs, each kernel pair under the correspondence alignment proposed), and what the rerun on the same proof cache took from the first run:

| Part | Kind | Verdict | On the rerun | Why not verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /quotes` | entry point | refuted | an exact hit |  |
| `POST /quotes/text` | entry point | unresolved | not a proof | `what the analysis can't see stays unresolved: the old build: a dynamic call site the walk doesn't follow: StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants in QuotesController.quoteText(long, int) (string concatenation: the string's value isn't modeled); the new build: a dynamic call site the walk doesn't follow: StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants in QuotesController.quoteText(long, int) (string concatenation: the string's value isn't modeled)` |
| `shop.Pricing#discount` | kernel | verified | an exact hit |  |
| `shop.Pricing#total` | kernel | refuted | an exact hit; `Pricing.discount` proved on its own and taken as one function |  |
| `shop.Pricing#withQuantity` | kernel | verified | an exact hit |  |
| `shop.Money#cents (was shop.Quote#cents)` | kernel | unresolved | not a proof | `class not found in the previous version: shop.Money` |
| `shop.Quote#quantity` | kernel | unresolved | not a proof | `the receiver is made differently in the two versions: this: a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(cents: long, quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts before, this: a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(amount: Money(cents: long), quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts now; a receiver of another construction or other fields is not supported yet` |

Obligations, one per observation of an old entry point: 7 preserved, 1 unresolved. Decisions a person made, by category: approved exclusion 0, domain restriction 0, environment assumption 0, mapping 0, observation change 0.

No question is left for a person.

- every modeled call returns normally, the environment model's only outcome: a failure of a store, broker or client is outside the claim

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

Yes, in this repo: `QuotesControllerTest.answersTheTextRouteWithTheTotal`, `QuotesControllerTest.quotesASmallOrderAtFullPrice`, `QuotesControllerTest.sendsNothingForAFreeQuote`, `QuotesControllerTest.takesATenthOffTenItemsOrMore` fails (`java -ea shop.Tests`). That test was written for this property. The contract needed no one to anticipate it.

## Why it matters

A proof of a reshaped object needs a relation between the old and new objects, and a tool that infers one could pick whichever makes the proof go through. Here `old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents + 1` does: the totals agree under it on every input. The regression is then explained away, not found.

## Why the verdict is right

Alignment proposes only equations that copy a field into the field it was routed to, never arithmetic, so `old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents` is the only candidate, and the request's inputs at the route are anchored by its observation spec, so no mapping is involved there at all. Under them, `total` returns 0 before and 1 after for a quote of 0 cents and one item, and `POST /quotes` answers 0 and sends nothing before, 1 and a `QuoteEvent(total=1, quantity=1)` after.

## What to do

Remove the extra cent. The app's tests catch this one too (four of five fail): the point of the example is that no automation layer of the run can hide it.

## Notes

- Checked by `jvmcontract compare`, which build.py runs as the B9 check of the shop app (`run_tool_compare`): the unpatched build against the patched one, twice under one fresh proof cache, the verdict read from the rerun and the page's output from the first run. The verdict is the subject's; the page lists every other part the run checked.
- The joint example of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md`'s Phase 5, made an example: the app's sources are the fixture's `before` build (`lib/tests/fixtures/foundations/`), and the patch turns them into its `after` build with the offset defect (`defects/offset/`) overlaid. `lib/tests/compare.rs` holds `jvmcontract compare` to the same builds inline; this is the same run by build.py, with the app's tests run too.
- Nothing in the run is written by hand. The entry points' external inputs (`cents`, `quantity`) are anchored by their observation specs, so no mapping is involved at the boundary. The kernel's relation between the old and new quotes (`old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents`, `old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity`) is alignment's proposal, inferred from how the two constructors route their parameters into the fields; it stays *proposed*, its evidence the proof under its claim key, and since nothing external anchors a kernel method's inputs, a proved relation there is reported as proved and not as the intended one.
- What stays unresolved in every example of the set, by name: `POST /quotes/text` (its string concatenation isn't modeled), `Quote#cents` moved to `Money#cents` (a method of a class the old build doesn't have) and `Quote#quantity`, whose receiver is made differently in the two versions (`Quote(long, int)` before, `Quote(Money, int)` now), which the regression check doesn't relate yet. Before the application-core merge (2026-11-08) it was refused as an instance method instead; the merge's check takes a receiver made by its constructor, of the same construction in both versions.
- Run inline on 2026-11-07 (JDK 25.0.5), `jvmcontract compare` on the app compiled unpatched and patched, as build.py compiles it, and on the fixture's builds, with the same verdicts (the times are the fixture's): `POST /quotes` refuted on `cents=0, quantity=1` and `Pricing#total` refuted on `new Quote(new Money(0), 1)`, both replayed on a JVM; `withQuantity` and `discount` verified. 1.5 s cold; the rerun took 0.2 s, the refutations reused and their witnesses replayed again.
- `total`'s proof is made again, under a claim key of its own, not taken from 190's: the closure digests of the changed `total` differ (`lib/tests/compare.rs`).
